transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah. I guess I’ve been having a hard time with eating after work. I work as a cashier, and after my shifts I’ll stop and buy takeout—probably more than I really need. Like burgers, fries, chicken, dessert… kind of enough for a few people. And then I’ll sit there and eat almost all of it myself before I go home.

I know that probably sounds bad. I just… I thought I should come in and talk to someone about it.
After you eat that amount of food, do you ever make yourself vomit, take laxatives, or exercise a lot more than usual to try to balance it out?

Um… no, I don’t think so. I mean, I’m not making myself throw up or anything like that. And I don’t take laxatives.

Exercise… not really. I might tell myself I should walk more or “be better” the next day, but I don’t, like, do some huge workout to make up for it. Is that what you mean?
When you're eating that large amount of food, do you ever feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but… yes. Once I take that first bite, it’s like something kind of shuts off in me.

I’ll be thinking, like, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” but my hands just keep going to the next thing anyway. It’s embarrassing to say, but in the moment it really doesn’t feel like I’m choosing it the way I should be.
Does this eating behavior cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

Yeah… I mean, I’m still making it to work and everything, so it’s not like I’m totally falling apart. But… it does bother me a lot.

I’m spending money on food that we really don’t have to spare, and then I don’t always tell my wife the truth about it. Or I kind of hide how much I bought. And that just makes things at home feel… tense, I guess. Like I’m being dishonest, which I don’t want to be. Does that make sense?
How often would you say this pattern of eating happens—like, how many times a week or month?

Um… I guess it’s more than I’d like to admit. For the last several months, it’s been… probably three or four nights most weeks.

I keep wanting to say it’s not every week, but honestly, since the foreclosure calls started, I can’t really remember a week where it didn’t happen at least once. Is that… the kind of number you mean?
Have you ever tried any other methods, like fasting for the next day or doing a lot more physical activity than usual, to make up for the food you ate during these episodes?

I don’t think so… not really.

I mean, sometimes the next day I might tell myself I’m going to “be good” or eat lighter, but I don’t really have, like, a plan or anything. And I’m not going out and exercising a bunch to make up for it. I’m usually just… kind of ashamed and trying to get through the day, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed this affecting your mood, relationships, or ability to function at work or home in any other ways?

I mean… work-wise, I still show up for my cashier shifts. I don’t think I’ve, like, stopped functioning or anything.

But at home, yeah… it’s causing problems. I’m spending money on food when we really don’t have extra, and then I end up hiding it or not being totally honest with my wife. I hate saying that, but it’s true. It makes things feel tense, like I’m keeping secrets. I guess that’s probably not great, right?
Have you ever fasted, severely restricted your food intake, or done anything else to try to control your weight or make up for the food you ate during these episodes?

Not really… I mean, I might think, like, “Okay, tomorrow I’ll try to eat less,” but I don’t usually follow through in any serious way.

I haven’t fasted or, um, done anything extreme to make up for it. At least I don’t think so. Mostly I just feel bad about it and try to act normal the next day. Is that what you mean?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with your family?

Um… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say hopeless, exactly. I mean, I get embarrassed and kind of down on myself after, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing.

I still like being with my family and stuff. Maybe I’m not always in the best mood, but I wouldn’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that… does that answer it?
Do you usually eat this large amount of food in secret, or do you feel embarrassed about others seeing you eat this way?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t really like people seeing it. I usually try to keep it private.

Sometimes I’ll eat in the parking lot before I come home, or I’ll wait until my wife’s asleep. And then I’ll kind of… hide the bags or receipts, like shove them down in the trash so she doesn’t see how much it was.

It sounds bad saying it out loud. I’m not trying to be sneaky exactly, I just feel really ashamed about it.
Do you feel like these eating episodes affect your ability to be fully present with your family or cause you to withdraw from social situations?

Yeah… I mean, I still go to work and do my cashier shifts, so it’s not like I’m completely falling apart or anything.

But at home, I guess it does get in the way. I spend money on food that we really shouldn’t be spending, and then I’m trying to hide it or not talk about it with my wife. So I’m there with my family, but sometimes I’m kind of distracted or tense because I’m worried she’ll notice.

I don’t like admitting that. It makes things feel… dishonest, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you ever done anything else, maybe not involving exercise or laxatives, to try to make up for the food you ate during these episodes—like skipping meals for a day or using diet pills?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like diet pills or anything like that.

I mean, I might tell myself I’m going to “be good” the next day, or eat lighter, but I don’t really have some plan where I skip the whole day to make up for it. At least… not that I’d call it that.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
After these eating episodes, do you often feel guilty, depressed, or disgusted with yourself?

I mean… yeah, I don’t feel great after. I usually feel pretty ashamed, like, “Why did I do that again?” But I don’t know if I’d say depressed exactly.

Disgusted is a strong word… but sometimes, yeah, kind of. I try not to think about it too much because then I just feel worse. Is that what you mean?
During these episodes, do you feel like you’re not fully in control of your eating, like you can’t stop even if you want to?

Yeah… I think that’s probably the part that bothers me the most.

I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but once I take that first bite, it’s like something in me kind of clicks off. I’ll be thinking, “Demetrius, stop, you don’t need any more,” but then my hands are still reaching for the next thing anyway.

So… yeah, I guess it does feel like I’m not really in control in those moments.
